title: Stoichiometry: Core Mole Concepts and Solutions - Worksheet 3
topic: Mole Calculations, Gas Volumes, Concentrations, and Ion Ratios
subject: Pure Chemistry

questions.question:
What is the mass of a 0.25 mol sample of anhydrous sodium carbonate, Na₂CO₃?
[Relative atomic masses: C = 12, O = 16, Na = 23]
questions.explanation: The molar mass (Mr) of Na₂CO₃ = (23 x 2) + 12 + (16 x 3) = 106 g per mol. Mass = Number of moles x Molar mass = 0.25 mol x 106 g per mol = 26.50 g.

questions.question:
What volume is occupied by 11.0 g of carbon dioxide gas (CO₂) at room temperature and pressure (r.t.p.)?
[Relative atomic masses: C = 12, O = 16; Molar volume of gas = 24 dm³ per mol at r.t.p.]
questions.explanation: Mr of CO₂ = 12 + (16 x 2) = 44 g per mol. Number of moles of CO₂ = 11.0 g divided by 44 g per mol = 0.25 mol. Volume of gas = Moles x Molar volume = 0.25 mol x 24 dm³ per mol = 6.0 dm³.

questions.question:
A student dissolves 4.0 g of sodium hydroxide (NaOH) pellets in distilled water to prepare a 250 cm³ solution. What is the concentration of this solution in mol per dm³?
[Relative atomic masses: H = 1, O = 16, Na = 23]
questions.explanation: Mr of NaOH = 23 + 16 + 1 = 40 g per mol. Moles of NaOH = 4.0 g divided by 40 g per mol = 0.10 mol. Volume in dm³ = 250 cm³ divided by 1000 = 0.25 dm³. Concentration = Moles divided by Volume = 0.10 mol divided by 0.25 dm³ = 0.40 mol per dm³.

questions.question:
A 0.10 mol sample of a pure divalent metal oxide with the chemical formula MO has an exact mass of 4.0 g. Identify the element M.
[Relative atomic mass: O = 16]
questions.explanation: Molar mass (Mr) of MO = Mass divided by Moles = 4.0 g divided by 0.10 mol = 40 g per mol. Since Mr of MO = Ar of M + 16, we set up the equation: Ar of M + 16 = 40, which yields Ar of M = 24. Looking at the periodic table, the element with an Ar of 24 is Magnesium.

questions.question:
Calculate the percentage by mass of nitrogen present in a pure sample of ammonium nitrate fertilizer, NH₄NO₃.
[Relative atomic masses: H = 1, N = 14, O = 16]
questions.explanation: Mr of NH₄NO₃ = 14 + (1 x 4) + 14 + (16 x 3) = 80 g per mol. There are two nitrogen atoms in the formula unit, so the mass of nitrogen = 14 x 2 = 28 g. Percentage by mass = (28 divided by 80) x 100% = 35.0%.

questions.question:
An unknown gaseous hydrocarbon is analyzed and found to contain 85.7% carbon by mass. If a quantitative sample of this gas contains exactly 3.0 moles of carbon atoms, how many moles of hydrogen atoms are present in that same sample?
[Relative atomic masses: H = 1, C = 12]
questions.explanation: Percentage of Hydrogen = 100% - 85.7% = 14.3%. Mole calculation: Moles of C = 85.7 divided by 12 = 7.14 mol. Moles of H = 14.3 divided by 1 = 14.3 mol. The simplistic mole ratio C : H is 7.14 : 14.3, which reduces to 1 : 2. If there are 3.0 moles of carbon atoms, there must be double the amount of hydrogen atoms: 3.0 x 2 = 6.0 moles.

questions.question: What is the total number of moles of ions present in 200 cm³ of an aqueous aluminium sulfate solution, Al₂(SO₄)₃, with a concentration of 0.50 mol per dm³?
questions.explanation: Moles of Al₂(SO₄)₃ solute = Concentration x Volume = 0.50 mol per dm³ x (200 divided by 1000) dm³ = 0.10 mol. Each formula unit of Al₂(SO₄)₃ fully dissociates into 2 Al³⁺ ions and 3 SO₄²⁻ ions, giving 5 ions in total. Total moles of dissolved ions = 0.10 mol x 5 = 0.50 mol.

questions.question:
A 1.20 g sample of a reactive Group II metal X reacts fully with excess hydrochloric acid. The reaction liberates 720 cm³ of hydrogen gas measured at r.t.p. Identify metal X.
[Molar volume of gas = 24 dm³ per mol at r.t.p.]
questions.explanation: The general equation is X + 2HCl -> XCl₂ + H₂. Moles of H₂ gas released = (720 divided by 1000) divided by 24 = 0.030 mol. Based on the 1:1 mole ratio, moles of metal X consumed = 0.030 mol. Relative atomic mass (Ar) of X = Mass divided by Moles = 1.20 g divided by 0.030 mol = 40. The Group II element with an Ar of 40 is Calcium.

questions.question:
An aqueous solution of sulfuric acid (H₂SO₄) has a concentration of 4.9 g per dm³. Express this concentration value in units of mol per dm³.
[Relative atomic masses: H = 1, S = 32, O = 16]
questions.explanation: The molar mass (Mr) of H₂SO₄ = (1 x 2) + 32 + (16 x 4) = 98 g per mol. To convert concentration from g per dm³ to mol per dm³, divide by the molar mass: 4.9 g per dm³ divided by 98 g per mol = 0.05 mol per dm³.

questions.question: A student mixes 100 cm³ of 0.20 mol per dm³ NaCl solution with 100 cm³ of 0.10 mol per dm³ CaCl₂ solution. Assuming volumes are additive, what is the final concentration of chloride ions (Cl⁻) in the mixed solution?
questions.explanation: Moles of Cl⁻ from NaCl = 0.100 dm³ x 0.20 mol per dm³ = 0.020 mol. Moles of Cl⁻ from CaCl₂ = 0.100 dm³ x 0.10 mol per dm³ x 2 = 0.020 mol (since each CaCl₂ releases 2 Cl⁻). Total moles of Cl⁻ = 0.020 + 0.020 = 0.040 mol. Total mixed volume = 100 + 100 = 200 cm³ = 0.200 dm³. Concentration of Cl⁻ = 0.040 mol divided by 0.200 dm³ = 0.20 mol per dm³.
